title: rotation fanout delay causes transient org-scope loss
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported intermittent 401/403s during API key rotation windows. The failures correlated with leader/fanout propagation delays of rotated apikey metadata to downstream auth proxies, causing requests to be evaluated against stale org-scoping data. Impact window was typically 15s-90s depending on region and load. This ticket tracks the root cause, the emergency mitigation we applied, and the longer-term fix that is in review.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a test org with long-running streaming and short-lived session traffic patterns (mix of short API calls and streaming).
2) Trigger API key rotation for the org (simulate both manual rotation and automatic scheduled rotation).
3) Observe auth service leader applying rotation and fanout to edge proxies; under load, some proxies receive update latencies > 30s.
4) During the propagation window, send requests using the new key to proxies that haven't applied the rotation and observe 401/403 or org-mismatch errors (depending on cache state).

5) Reproduce on Dedicated by rotating keys via the control plane while saturating inter-zone network links; observe similar timeouts and auth rejects in Private (VPC) where control-plane reachability is intermittently delayed.
mitigation: 1) Rolled a temporary fallback in edge auth: allow 'new-key' acceptance on any proxy if the global rotation event timestamp is within the last 120s (safe-guarded by additional signed nonce checks).
2) Increased rotation fanout parallelism for Dedicated control-plane workers for the emergency window to reduce worst-case propagation times from ~90s to ~8s for affected customers.
3) Notified impacted customers and recommended immediate local retry/backoff updates in client SDKs (short-term guidance).
root_cause_summary: Rotation fanout uses a single-leader-driven serial propagation to zone-edge proxies; under high write/rotation throughput and transient network congestion (observed on a subset of Dedicated zones and Private peering paths) the leader's fanout loop degraded to sequential RPC retries. This caused a tail of proxies with stale apikey->org mappings. The auth evaluation code treats missing mapping as deny rather than consult fallback, so requests landed as 401/403 until mapping arrived.
fix_summary: Primary fix: make fanout idempotent and parallel with bounded concurrency and exponential backoff for individual proxy retries; add a fast-path for 'rotation-in-progress' checks at edge that consult a signed ledger of recent rotations instead of failing on missing mapping. Patch implements both kernel and config changes and includes defensive tests. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2847
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests simulating rotation fanout under induced network delays pass in CI.
Canary rollout to 10% of Hosted traffic (low-risk orgs) shows no 401 spike during scheduled rotations for 48h.
Dedicated smoke test harness validates <5s median propagation and <15s p95 for rotations under synthetic load.
Private deployment upgrade playbook validated in one customer air-gapped lab without auth regressions.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR and run full CI (runtime + auth proxy matrix).
2) Deploy to staging; run rotation stress suite for 6 hours.
3) Canary to 10% Hosted; monitor 401/403 rate, rotation ledger latency and fanout tail metrics for 48h.
4) Apply Dedicated upgrade to non-production pools, then progressively to production pools over 24h with automated rollback on >2x baseline 401s.
5) Offer Private customers a coordinated upgrade window and provide the upgrade bundle + playbook.
qa_plan: Add a harness that runs 1k concurrent rotation events across simulated proxies and asserts no auth rejects for keys within the acceptance window.
Run chaos tests that drop peering packets between control plane and a subset of proxies to verify fallback ledger path prevents denies.
Manual verification with two impacted customers: ingest production-like traffic and confirm no elevated auth failures during rotation.
monitoring: Alert: rotation.fanout.p99 > 30s for >3m triggers paging to SRE and auto-rollback of rotation-exposed flags.
Dashboards: auth/401-rate by org during rotation windows; probe per-proxy mapping-age histogram.
